name: Primary Orthostatic Tremor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Orthostatic Tremor

criteria.description: Presence of high-frequency (13-18 Hz) tremor in leg muscles upon standing detected by electromyography
Subjective sensation of unsteadiness or tremor appearing immediately upon standing and relieved by sitting or walking
No evidence of other neurological disorders causing tremor or gait instability
Normal brain MRI excluding alternative diagnoses
Clinical improvement of tremor symptoms with clonazepam treatment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Electromyography is essential to confirm the characteristic high-frequency tremor.

imaging: Normal brain MRI excluding structural lesions
other: Electromyography showing 13-18 Hz synchronous tremor in leg muscles upon standing

distinguishingFeatures: Tremor present during action and posture, not specifically on standing
Absence of immediate unsteadiness upon standing
Irregular, jerky movements rather than rhythmic tremor
Lower frequency and variable EMG pattern
Often associated with other neurological signs

redFlags: Presence of other neurological deficits (e.g., weakness, sensory loss)
references: Gerschlager W, Brown P. Orthostatic tremor: clinical and electrophysiological features. Mov Disord. 2005.
McManis PG, et al. Primary orthostatic tremor: clinical and electrophysiological features. Neurology. 1993.
